title: Port mapping in Docker
idea: Port mapping publishes a container's private port on a port of your host, so traffic from outside can reach the app inside.

analogy.text: An office building with a switchboard. Callers dial the main number and extension; the desk phone inside has no outside line of its own.
analogy.breaks: Each host port can be published by only one container.

points: Each container has its own network namespace, so its ports are private.
`-p HOST:CONTAINER` publishes a container port on a host port.
`EXPOSE` in a Dockerfile documents a port; it does not publish it.
Two containers can use one container port if their host ports differ.

parts.label: Command
parts.note: Creates a container from an image and starts it.

parts.label: Publish flag
parts.note: Asks Docker to forward a host port into the container.

parts.label: Host port
parts.note: The port on your machine. Clients connect here, for example localhost:8080.

parts.label: Separator
parts.note: Host on the left, container on the right. Never swap them.

parts.label: Container port
parts.note: The port your app listens on inside the container.

parts.label: Image
parts.note: The image to start. Its name comes last.

code.caption: Two containers from one image, both listening on 3000 inside, reached on different host ports.

walk.text: Run `shop` detached. Host port 8080 forwards to port 3000 in the container.
Same image, same container port 3000, but host port 8081. No clash.
Request the first container through the host port 8080.
Request the second container through 8081. Each answer comes from a different container.
Ask Docker which host port maps to `shop-a`'s published port.

pitfalls: Write `-p HOST:CONTAINER` in that order; `-p 3000:8080` publishes container port 8080.
Make your app listen on `0.0.0.0`; `127.0.0.1` inside the container stays unreachable.
Pick a free host port; a second container on 8080 fails to start.

quiz.q: The app listens on 3000 in the container. Which flag serves it at localhost:9000?
quiz.why: The host port comes first and the container port second. `EXPOSE` only documents a port, and `-p 9000` names a container port.

takeaway: Use -p HOST:CONTAINER to open a container's private port to your host.

starters: Why does localhost not work from inside a container?
How do I let Docker pick a free host port?
